name: Art Deco tableware
summary: Bright, hand-painted earthenware in angles, cones and bands. Painters in the potteries of Stoke-on-Trent put bold flat colour on a white ground, and the shapes copy the stepped and conical forms of the Paris fair of 1925.

philosophy.core_thesis: A cheap white earthenware becomes modern when a painter puts strong flat colour in sharp geometry on a form with angles and cones.
design_principles: Form the piece in a sharp geometry: a cone, a step, a square or a triangle handle.
Paint in flat enamel colours: orange, yellow, red, green and black, with no shading.
Divide the surface with bands 3 to 10 mm wide, in bold stripes or in steps.
Paint a motif in a few strokes: a crocus, a sun ray, a tree, or a house, and repeat it.
Use a white or cream ground, and a thin clear glaze that gives a bright gloss.
Let the hand show: each stroke has a small variation, though the pattern is a fixed design.
Give each pattern a bold name and put it on the base with the maker mark.
anti_patterns: A soft pastel painting in the Rococo manner
A gilt rim and a botanical flower
A printed pattern in blue on white
A round, curvy and pale organic form

form.shape: Conical sugar shakers and cruets, plates with a square or stepped rim, angular jugs and tureens, and stacked bowls.
form.profile: A cone, a cube or a stepped profile; the handle is a flat triangle or a solid ring.
form.foot_and_rim: A flat, plain base; the rim is a sharp edge or a stepped edge, with a painted band.
form.proportion: Plate diameter 18 to 25 cm and wall 4 to 6 mm thick; the colour bands cover about two thirds of the surface.
rules: Build the form from 2 or 3 simple solids, such as a cone on a disc.
Make the handle a flat triangle or a solid ring, with no curl.
Paint the colour in flat bands that follow the form.

bodies.rule: Use a white earthenware that takes a bright flat colour. Bone china is for the costly lines. Do not use a brown stoneware: the colour needs a white ground.

methods: hand painting with a brush in flat colour
lithographic transfer for the cheap lines
forming.joins: Triangle handles are cast with the body or luted with slip; stacking lids sit on a rebated seat.
forming.details: A small run of glaze at a band edge, a pattern name in the base, and a slight difference of stroke between pieces.

glaze.pattern: Crocus flowers, sunrays, orange trees, houses and diamond shapes in flat enamel colour, with broad bands and stripes.
glaze.wear: The enamel can scratch; the glaze may craze in a fine net, and the colour stays strong.

palette.strategy: A white ground with orange, yellow, red, green and black in flat blocks; the contrast between the colours is high.

firing.kiln: A coal or gas-fired bottle kiln; a biscuit firing, a glaze firing and a low enamel firing.
firing.scale: A painting shop of some hundreds of young women, who painted the same pattern to a fixed design.
firing.signs: A flat enamel colour with a slight edge, a pattern name in the base, and a small run at the band.

pieces.form: Conical sugar and pepper shaker in orange and yellow bands
Plate with a crocus motif in flat blue, orange and yellow
Small plate with black and orange bands and a gilt line on the rim
Stepped, square-sided bowl with a lithographic border of diamonds

positive: hand-painted flat enamel bands in orange yellow and black

evidence.title: Clarice Cliff conical coffee pot, Bizarre
Clarice Cliff Bizarre teapot, Newport Pottery, 1929

emotion.target_response: A bright, modern cheer: the viewer sees strong colour in sharp bands on a white plate and thinks of a new, fast and happy age.

use_cases: a museum label on Art Deco pottery
avoid_when: the brief wants soft pastel or gilt painting
the brief wants a plain minimal form
the brief wants a rustic hand-thrown look

modifiers.how: Drop the painted bands and the motif, change to white porcelain, and keep the simple solids.
Drop the pattern and glaze each piece in one strong colour, with rings in relief.
Change to bone china and add gilt bands and a painted flower.

wall_thickness.note: Earthenware is thicker than bone china; the colour bands hide the weight.
